title: Auricore Labs - weekly pilot results & tuning
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review latest pilot results: tokens/sec/$ improved after KV prefix caching and conservative batching changes; observed 18% cost saving from cache hit tuning but a 12ms p50 latency increase on long sequences. SE to run focused 48-hour throughput run with new batch profile; AE to send updated pricing/benchmarks; customer to validate SSO and SOC2 notes. Agreed next steps and owners.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-11 10:00 PST | Duration 50m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Auricore Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Auricore Eng Manager), Lena Kowalski (Auricore SRE)

[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick sanity check, can you all hear me?
[00:05] Priya: Yeah, loud and clear, thanks.
[00:07] Tom: Yep.
[00:10] Maya: Cool. Agenda for 30-ish minutes: quick results recap, the caching/batching tweaks Diego rolled out, then recs and next steps. We'll leave some time for security questions.
[00:20] Diego: Okay, I'll start. Over the last run we adjusted two knobs: prefix/KV caching thresholds and dynamic batch window sizes. The headline is tokens per dollar improved from ~1,200 to ~1,420 on average across our dev traces — about an 18% uplift when cache hit rates are at or above 42%.
[00:40] Priya: Wait, is that tokens per dollar or tokens per second? Need to be clear for finance.
[00:45] Diego: Yes sorry, tokens per dollar (tokens/$). We also measured tokens/sec/$ which moved from ~0.95 to 1.12 under sustained traffic. The improvement is mostly from reduced repeated prefix work — the K-V cash, oh sorry, KV cache hit rate.
[01:05] Tom: Nice. What was the impact on latency? We can't let p95 jump too much.
[01:09] Diego: Good point. p50 increased by roughly 12ms on long seqs (>1,024 tokens) after we increased batch window from 8ms to 25ms to capture more batching. p95 saw a marginal ~35ms uptick for those long tails. For median short requests (<256) there was negligible change.
[01:35] Priya: So it's a cost vs latency tradeoff — how much cost do we save vs how much latency we accept?
[01:40] Maya: Exactly. Our recommendation was conservative: keep batch window at 18ms in production, B3 profile on dedicated nodes, and enable prefix caching for sessions with repeat prompts. That got us the ~15-18% cost improvement while keeping p95 within their stated SLO of 350ms.
[02:05] Lena: Our concern is session affinity and cache consistency across pods. If a user is routed to a different GPU pool, do we lose the benefit?
[02:14] Diego: Right now cache is node-local KV. For our pilot we allowed sticky routing for warm sessions to the same pool; that recovers ~90% of hit-rate benefits. Full global KV would need extra infra and add write/replication complexity. We can do a multi-region cache plan later.
[02:35] Tom: That sticky routing — does it affect failover? If a node goes down we need fallback policy.
[02:40] Diego: We have automatic fallback to a cold model variant (smaller context) and fallback routing to another pool with slightly higher cost but we limit failover frequency. We log and chart any fallback events in Console.
[02:55] Priya: Can you show the numbers per seq length? Our distribution is bimodal — short chat queries ~180 tokens and document extracts ~2.2k tokens.
[03:05] Diego: Sure; on our sample: short bucket (<256) tokens/$ ~1,600, mid bucket (256-1024) ~1,300, long bucket (>1024) ~780. That's why long sequences drag down the average.
[03:25] Priya: Hmm that long bucket is the problem. Any options for them besides batching?
[03:29] Maya: Two levers: quantized model variants (reduce cost per token) or sequence chunking + recombine (app-level change). Diego: also prefix caching helps if the long requests share leading context.
[03:40] Tom: Did you try q4_0 or q2 variants in the pilot?
[03:44] Diego: We tried q4_0 on a replica. It shaved ~22% cost for long seqs with a slight quality delta on extraction tasks. We noted quality regression on some edge-case prompts — we flagged those in the eval set.
[03:58] Priya: Quality regression is sensitive for us. We need evals before any model change.
[04:02] Maya: Agreed. We'll keep the main pilot on the float model while Diego runs an ablation on q4_0 and reports delta metrics (ROUGE/F1) for your eval set.
[04:14] Priya: Ok. Regarding security, did you get the SOC2 packet?
[04:18] Maya: Yes, sent last week — there's a link in the meeting notes. But quick bits: audit logs retention, SSO/SAML support, and KMS integration for keys.
[04:30] Lena: We need to see sample audit events for prompt-level logging — and ensure PII masking can be applied pre-ingest.
[04:36] Diego: We have a pre-ingest filter in the pipeline for masking; we can add a sample sanitized log for you.
[04:43] Tom: Any legal red flags noticed?
[04:45] Maya: Nothing major so far. Procurement asked about data residency and we confirmed region pinning is possible in Dedicated. We'll add that to the one-pager.
[04:58] Priya: Back to economics — what's the projected tokens/sec/$ if we do both caching + q4_0?
[05:03] Diego: Combined best-case on our traces: short bucket ~1,900 tokens/$, mid ~1,650, long ~1,050. Overall blended ~1,550 tokens/$. But that's optimistic; we need the longer run test.
[05:20] Maya: So agreed actions: SE to run a 48-hour sustained run with B3 batch profile, sticky routing enabled, and a q4_0 replica for comparison. Upload sheet with tokens/sec/$ by bucket and latency percentiles.
[05:34] Priya: We'll also give you our production-like prompt mix and the 95th seq length.
[05:38] Tom: And CORS? small infra Q: will our SRE need to open different ports for private deployment?
[05:44] Diego: For Dedicated you just need to allow TLS egress to the control plane and internal gRPC between pools if you enable cross-pool replication. We'll send a network diagram.
[05:55] Lena: Please include the audit log schema — we want to map it to Splunk.
[06:00] Maya: Noted.
[06:02] [pause, typing sounds]
[06:10] Priya: One more thing — competitor question. We did a quick bench vs ModelServeX, they quoted lower latency but no prefix caching or the same dev experience. Thoughts?
[06:20] Maya: ModelServeX often trades off observability and rollout tooling for speed claims. Our differentiation is the predictable economics and caching/batching toolkit that reduces real costs for repeated prompts. We'll send a short comparison doc.
[06:34] Diego: Also, ModelServeX didn't have our auto-fallback to cheaper variants; that matters for 24/7 availability.
[06:42] Priya: Good to know.
[06:45] Maya: Any blockers on your side for the run?
[06:48] Priya: We'll share the prompt mix by Monday. Need the one-pager and the spreadsheet.
[06:54] Maya: I'll send the one-pager and the sheet today. Diego will start the 48-hour run early tomorrow.
[06:58] Tom: Timeline OK.
[07:00] Maya: Awesome. Recap: Diego runs 48h and uploads, Maya sends pricing + bench sheet, Priya provides prompt mix, Lena confirms SSO/audit details. We'll reconvene next Thursday unless the run triggers a deep-dive.
[07:18] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[07:20] Maya: Thanks, bye.

Notes/links mentioned: shared sheet: https://redwood.example.com/sheets/auricore-pilot-bench (placeholder), SOC2 packet link, network diagram stub.

End of transcript.
